p01.why: The inherited copy candidate deduces Derived<int> from a Base<int> object, and Derived<int> has no constructor that takes a Base<int>; Clang finds no guide at all, so every compiler rejects.

p02.why: A guide must be declared in the scope of its class template, and this one is at global scope for lib::Box.

p03.why: T&& is an rvalue reference that takes 1 and gives T = int; U&& is a forwarding reference that takes the lvalue i.

p04.why: The alias names the class template after a dependent qualifier, so it must have its arguments.

p05.why: A trailing pack of bases takes the remaining elements, giving Overloads<ByInt, ByDouble>.

p06.why: The first element fixes the pack to X, Y, Z; the empty lists give no deduction and agree.

p07.why: A pack before x takes no element, so the pack is empty.

p08.why: A dependent qualifier before the name is allowed, and deduction gives In<int> after instantiation (Q-0243).

p09.why: For 3 the non-template user guide beats the template guide Size(T) and gives Size<long>; for 'a' Size(T) is an exact match and gives Size<char>.

p10.why: The guide's result must be a template-id of the class template it names.

p11.why: A guide must have no body.

p12.why: T is only in a non-deduced position, so no guide gives T.

p13.why: Only the copy candidate gives T, so Box<int>.

p14.why: The braces of the dependent member In<T> stay; the non-dependent Plain has its braces elided, so 3L goes to z.

p15.why: a sees no user guide and gets Box<long>; for b the later user guide ties with Box(T) and wins as a user guide.

p16.why: The braces of In<T> are not elided, so two elements for one member give no aggregate candidate and no guide fits.

p17.why: The first element fixes the pack, X{} matches X, and Y and Z get empty lists.

p18.why: The fixed char v[3] takes "ab", and 1 deduces T = int; EDG forms no candidate here (Q-0277).

p19.why: Each form copies one, and a braced single element of the class skips the initializer-list phase.

p20.why: The name without arguments must not be part of an array declarator.

p21.why: T is deduced as int and long, so no guide is viable.

p22.why: The guide's result has a cv-qualifier; GCC accepts (Q-0242).

p23.why: The constant parameter's type is deduced from each argument, so Wrap<int> and Wrap<char>.

p24.why: Through Same, T is deduced as int and char.

p25.why: A guide must have no specifier other than explicit.

p26.why: T&& of a class parameter is no forwarding reference, so it does not bind the lvalue n.

p27.why: With an argument list there is no deduction and U takes the default int, so second is 2.

p28.why: The two guides tie because the defaulted parameter is not compared, and the guide from the non-template Mark(T), not explicit, wins.

p29.why: Derived<int> is deduced from the Base<int> object, but no constructor of Derived<int> takes it; every compiler rejects.

p30.why: Each listed place allows the bare name, and the deduced types are as asserted.

p31.why: The own explicit Derived(T) guide ties with the inherited user guide and wins by the first tie-breaker, and an explicit guide is chosen in copy-list initialization.

p32.why: Y stands where X is fixed by the first element.

p33.why: An array with a dependent element type and a fixed bound has its braces elided, so Three<int>, Three<const char*>, and Mixed<int>.

p34.why: The own explicit constructor-template guide ties with the inherited Base(T) guide and wins by CTAD-19, before CTAD-22; it is explicit in copy-list initialization.

p35.why: A parenthesized list in new has an aggregate candidate, giving Agg<int>; GCC forms none (Q-0244).

p36.why: A parenthesized list also gives the aggregate candidate with the fixed pack; GCC forms none (Q-0352).

p37.why: With no initializer, no guide takes zero arguments.

p38.why: Through Same, both arguments give T = int.

p39.why: U gets no value from the guide's parameters and has no default; every compiler rejects when it is used.

p40.why: The copy candidate wins the tie with the guide from the copy constructor.

p41.why: The array bound depends on N, so its braces are not elided and three elements for one member give no candidate.

p42.why: Specializations give no guides, and the primary's Shape(T) takes one argument.

p43.why: The guide from the non-template explicit Mark(T) wins the tie, and it is explicit in copy-list initialization.

p44.why: User guides apply to an undefined primary, so Only<int>, whose explicit specialization takes int.

p45.why: For Same, the constructor guide cannot take long for T*, and the user guide gives Pair<int*, long>, which is not a specialization of Same.

p46.why: The user guide ties with the copy candidate and wins, because CTAD-20 comes before CTAD-21, so Box<Box<int>>.

p47.why: c and d deduce Box<int> and Box<double> in one declaration.

p48.why: A template template parameter can stand for deduction after substitution (Q-0275).

p49.why: The bare name must not be a function parameter type.

p50.why: One element of the class or a derived class skips the initializer-list phase and copies; two elements or a long use the list guide.

p51.why: A pack before x takes no element, so Empty{} goes to int x and the list has more elements than members.

p52.why: A braced list gives an rvalue reference to T[N], and a string literal gives a const array reference, so int,3 and char,4.

p53.why: An empty list gives no aggregate candidate; the no-parameter guide leaves T to its default int.

p54.why: A parenthesized list gives the aggregate candidate with the trailing pack; GCC forms none for a pack of bases in parentheses (Q-0352).

p55.why: Copy-initialization with = leaves out the explicit guide, and no other guide fits.

p56.why: The fixed int and long positions take converted arguments, giving Pair<int, char> and Pair<long, char>; EDG and Clang 18 reject.

p57.why: The user guide wins deduction and gives Pair<int>, whose two constructors are ambiguous for (1, 2).

p58.why: A range-for variable and condition variables can use deduction.

p59.why: Derived inherits no constructors, so it gets no guides from Base, and the aggregate candidate cannot deduce Base<T> from 1.

p60.why: Two non-template guides have the same parameter types; EDG accepts (Q-0280).

p61.why: The bare name must not be part of a reference declarator.

p62.why: Deduction works through an alias of a template template parameter after substitution (Q-0275).

p63.why: The bare name must not be part of a pointer declarator.

p65.why: Indexed requires Offset<T>, and double* + double is not valid, so the guide for r is not viable.

p66.why: The user guide ties with the constructor guide and wins, so Box<long>.

p67.why: A user guide removes the aggregate candidate, and the user guide needs a pointer.

p68.why: Each constructor gives a guide; the defaults and the empty pack work, so Tuple e is Tuple<>.

p69.why: Derived(const T&) and the inherited Base(T) have different parameter types, so CTAD-19 does not apply and the guides tie; Clang has no inherited guide and accepts (Q-0239).

p70.why: sizeof(int) > 1 makes the guide explicit, and it is chosen in copy-list initialization.

p71.why: Deduction gives Gone<int>, and its constructor is deleted.

p72.why: The user guide wins the tie, so Wide<long long>.

p73.why: An alias template for a pointer type must have its arguments.

p74.why: Through the alias the user guide gives Box<int>, the copy candidate Box<char>, and the aggregate candidate Agg<int, char>; Clang 18 rejects.

p75.why: Through the alias one element of the class skips the initializer-list phase; EDG differs (Q-0279).

p76.why: U gets no value from the guide's parameters; Clang rejects the guide, GCC and EDG accept it unused (Q-0241).

p77.why: The inherited guides give Derived<int>; Clang makes no inherited guides and rejects (Q-0239).

p78.why: The two constructor-template guides give Box<char> and Box<int> and neither is more specialized.

p79.why: Direct initialization takes the more specialized explicit guide Box(T*); copy-initialization with = leaves it out and gets Box<int*>.

p80.why: The copy candidate wins over the copy constructor's guide.

p81.why: The braces of the dependent base Base<T> stay, so 1 cannot give Base<T>.

p82.why: Two user guide templates with the same parameters both take &i and neither is better.

p83.why: Two(T, int) and Two(int, T) both deduce int and neither is more specialized.

p84.why: A guide for a member template must have the access of that member, which is private.

p85.why: make and fixed are instantiated after the Box guide, and later<int> uses the guides before its first point of instantiation, so Cell<int> both times.

p86.why: Box<> takes the default, and Box(2.5) deduces double.

p87.why: The aggregate candidate works with braces, parentheses, and designators.

p88.why: Two elements for one member give no aggregate candidate.

p89.why: N gets no value and has no default; Clang rejects, GCC and EDG accept the unused guide (Q-0241).

p90.why: With the pack length fixed, ToY only converts to Y and does not deduce; GCC accepts (Q-0276).

p91.why: The no-parameter guide gives no value for T.

p92.why: The result must be a template-id of Box.

p93.why: A string literal gives the parameter const unsigned char(&)[N], which a const char[4] does not match.

p94.why: A public in-class guide for the member template gives Outer::In<int> through the qualified name.

p95.why: The own non-explicit Derived(T) guide wins over the inherited explicit one, so copy-list initialization is valid.

p96.why: e and f deduce Box<int> and Box<char> in one declaration.

p97.why: No initializer or an empty list uses the no-parameter guide and the default.

p98.why: Direct initialization chooses the more specialized explicit Pick(T*); copy-initialization leaves it out.

p99.why: Only the guide with U = int satisfies Wide, so Box<char>; Pad<int> meets the class constraint.

p100.why: A member alias of the class stands for T.

p101.why: T&& takes the rvalue 1 with T = int.

p102.why: Through the alias, T&& stays no forwarding reference and does not bind i; EDG accepts (Q-0278).

p103.why: The inherited user guide gives Derived<int>; Clang makes no inherited guides and rejects (Q-0239).

p104.why: The explicit guide Box(T*) is more specialized, wins, and is explicit in copy-list initialization.

p105.why: For char the guide is not explicit; direct-list initialization allows the explicit one for int.

p106.why: The braces of Base<T> stay, so {1} gives Base<int>.

p107.why: short matches Box(T) exactly; for int the non-template user guide wins.

p108.why: Both guides need Wide<char>, which fails, so no guide is viable.

p109.why: The bare name must not be a return type.

p110.why: The user guide's result Box<long> cannot match Box<T*>, so the constructor guide gives Box<int*>.

p111.why: The bare name must not be the type of a non-static member.

p112.why: A dependent qualifier with template is allowed; Clang rejects (Q-0243).

p113.why: The forwarding user guide gives Box<int&> and Box<int>; the non-template guide wins for the literal; defaults give Box<short> and Item<int>.

p114.why: The base Base<int> does not use T, so the inherited guides give no T, and nothing else fits.

p115.why: Copy-list initialization chooses the explicit guide.

p116.why: The private constructor's guide is usable and gives Secret<int>, but the initialization then picks the private constructor.

p117.why: Arguments with the exact fixed types deduce through both aliases; Clang 18 rejects.
